label: bug
file: src/export/scheduler.ts

`nextRunAt` handles the "daily" cadence correctly by checking whether today's run time has already passed before deciding whether to use today or tomorrow, but the "weekly" branch always does `next.setUTCDate(next.getUTCDate() + 7)` unconditionally. When a weekly schedule is created before RUN_HOUR_UTC (06:00 UTC) on its intended day, the computed `next` (today at 06:00) is still in the future relative to `from`, so the correct first run is today — but the code skips straight to +7 days, silently dropping the first week's export. This matches both reports: the schedule created at 05:40 UTC on a Monday missed that Monday's run, while one created at 09:00 UTC (after the run hour) happened to work because the next occurrence genuinely was 7 days out. The weekly branch needs the same "is this still in the future?" check the daily branch uses before adding 7 days.

input.title: Fix weekly scheduled exports skipping the first run
input.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

In `nextRunAt`, the "weekly" branch always advances the date by 7 days, unlike "daily" which only advances when the computed run time has already passed (`next <= from`). This means a weekly schedule created before `RUN_HOUR_UTC` on its run day unconditionally skips that day's run and jumps a full week ahead, even though the run time hasn't occurred yet. This matches the reported behavior: a schedule created at 05:40 UTC (before the 06:00 UTC run hour) sent nothing until the following week, while one created at 09:00 (after the run hour) worked as expected.

Propose changing the "weekly" case to mirror "daily": only add 7 days when `next <= from`, otherwise leave `next` as the computed same-day run time. This ensures a weekly schedule created before the daily run hour still fires on its intended first day instead of skipping to the following week.
